q: What is the standard normal human body temperature on the Celsius scale?
Which device tracks maximum and minimum daily atmospheric temperatures?
Define 'Temperature' and state its commonly used unit.
a: Temperature is a reliable quantitative measure of the degree of hotness or coldness of a body. Its common unit is degree Celsius (°C).

q: Why is human touch sensation unreliable for measuring temperature?
a: Touch is relative and depends on the prior condition of the hand, as shown when the same lukewarm water feels warm to a cold hand and cold to a warm hand.

q: What structural difference allows a clinical thermometer to be read outside the mouth while a laboratory thermometer cannot?
a: A clinical thermometer has a constriction (kink) in its capillary tube that prevents the mercury column from dropping when removed. A laboratory thermometer lacks a kink, so its mercury level drops immediately upon removal from the liquid.
